title: Multisource Coronary Artery Fistula Draining Into the Coronary Sinus: Multimodality Imaging and Surgical Repair.
abstract: Coronary artery fistula (CAF) is a rare congenital coronary anomaly. Multisource CAF draining into the coronary sinus is exceptionally uncommon and anatomically complex. A woman presented with progressive exertional dyspnea and right-sided heart failure. Multimodality imaging, including transthoracic echocardiography, coronary computed tomography angiography, and invasive coronary angiography, demonstrated multisource CAFs arising from the right coronary artery and left circumflex artery draining into the coronary sinus with diffuse aneurysmal coronary dilatation. The patient underwent surgical ligation of the dominant right CAF with concomitant tricuspid annuloplasty. Postoperative imaging demonstrated successful closure of the dominant right CAF with thrombus formation within the ligated fistulous tract, whereas the smaller left circumflex artery fistula persisted, and serial follow-up demonstrated clinical improvement. Multimodality imaging is essential for diagnosis, treatment planning, and postoperative surveillance of complex CAF. Surgical repair remains an effective treatment strategy for anatomically complex fistulas associated with significant hemodynamic consequences.

title: A deep learning radiomics model based on multiparametric MRI for predicting the efficacy of neoadjuvant chemotherapy in axillary lymph nodes of breast cancer.
abstract: Objectives In this study, we developed and validated a deep learning radiomics clinical (DLRC) model integrating multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) and clinical data to predict axillary pathological complete response (apCR) in cN+ breast cancer patients receiving neoadjuvant chemotherapy (NAC). Materials and methods We retrospectively collected data from 221 eligible breast cancer patients. The DLRC model integrated radiomics features and deep learning scores (DL-Scores) derived from mpMRI, together with clinical risk factors, to predict apCR. Seven classifiers were employed for model construction, and the optimal classifier was selected based on classification performance to build the final model. Model performance was evaluated using the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve, area under the curve (AUC), calibration curve, and decision curve analysis (DCA). Classification performance was assessed via the confusion matrix. Additionally, SHAP plots were utilized for interpretability analysis of the model. Results Multivariate analysis confirmed that progesterone receptor (PR), human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2), clinical T stage (OR = 0.258), and time-intensity curve (TIC) were significantly associated with apCR. The mpMRI based DLRC model achieved AUCs of 0.949 (95% CI, 0.912-0.986) and 0.932 (95% CI, 0.867-0.998) in the training and validation sets. SHAP analysis further revealed the interpretability of the model. The confusion matrix visually demonstrated the consistency between the predicted results and the true labels, validating the classification performance of the model. Conclusion The DLRC model effectively predicts apCR in breast cancer patients after NAC. It can serve as an auxiliary tool for clinicians in identifying potential candidates for axillary de-escalation, offering support for personalized precision treatment. We present this article in accordance with the TRIPOD-AI reporting checklist.

title: Atlas-assisted segment anything model for fetal brain MRI (FeTal-SAM).
abstract: This paper presents FeTal-SAM, a novel adaptation of the Segment Anything Model (SAM) tailored for fetal brain MRI segmentation. Traditional deep learning methods often require large annotated datasets for a fixed set of labels, making them inflexible when clinical or research needs change. By integrating atlas-based prompts and foundation-model principles, FeTal-SAM addresses two key limitations in fetal brain MRI segmentation: (1) the need to retrain models for varying label definitions, and (2) the lack of insight into whether segmentations are driven by genuine image contrast or merely inferred by learned spatial priors. We leverage multi-atlas registration to generate spatially aligned label templates that serve as dense prompts, alongside a bounding-box prompt, for SAM's segmentation decoder. This strategy enables binary segmentation on a per-structure basis, which is subsequently fused to reconstruct the full 3D segmentation volumes. Evaluations on two datasets, the dHCP dataset and an in-house dataset demonstrate FeTal-SAM's robust performance across gestational ages. Notably, it achieves Dice scores comparable to state-of-the-art baselines which were trained for each dataset and label definition for well-contrasted structures like cortical plate and cerebellum, while maintaining the flexibility to segment anatomical structures that could be templated by compatible atlas image and label sample pairs. Although slightly lower accuracy is observed for subtle, low-contrast structures (e.g., hippocampus, amygdala), our results highlight FeTal-SAM's potential as a flexible atlas-conditioned segmentation framework without requiring a separately trained model for each supported parcellation. This method thus constitutes a promising step toward clinically adaptable fetal brain MRI analysis tools.

title: Diagnostic performance and methodological heterogeneity of neuromelanin-sensitive MRI in Parkinson's disease: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) diagnosis remains primarily clinical and is often delayed until substantial neurodegeneration has occurred. Neuromelanin-sensitive MRI (NM-MRI) assesses the integrity of neuromelanin-rich nuclei affected in PD, the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNpc) and locus coeruleus (LC), but its diagnostic performance, technical determinants, and translational applicability remain unclear amid heterogeneity. We aimed to quantify diagnostic accuracy, determine whether performance varies across methodological approaches, and contextualise evidence from clinically relevant settings. We systematically reviewed NM-MRI diagnostic studies through December 2025. QUADAS-2 assessed risk of bias. Sensitivity and specificity were jointly pooled using a bivariate model, and AUC using random-effects meta-analysis. Subgroup analyses and exploratory meta-regressions assessed methodological heterogeneity; broader clinical evidence was synthesised qualitatively. Thirty-nine studies were included. Across 20 PD-versus-healthy-control (HC) studies (878 PD; 690 HCs), pooled sensitivity was 89.03% (95% CI 86.01-91.45%), specificity 87.02% (95% CI 82.76-90.34%), PLR 6.86, NLR 0.126, and DOR 54.37. Across 32 studies (1411 PD; 1086 HCs), pooled AUC was 0.909 (95% CI 0.884-0.929; I2 = 64.6%). No significant unadjusted differences emerged by sequence, dimensionality, segmentation, or measurement type. NM-MRI abnormalities were detectable across prodromal, early- and advanced-stage PD, although global measures showed limited discrimination between disease stages. Subregional measures captured phenotypic variation, genotype discrimination was limited, and PD-versus-ET/APS performance was promising but variable, within small, heterogeneous evidence bases. NM-MRI is a promising non-invasive imaging biomarker for PD, with strong discrimination across diverse methodological approaches. Harmonised acquisition and analysis, externally validated diagnostic thresholds, and prospective multicentre studies in clinically representative populations are needed to support future clinical implementation.

title: Predicting taste alteration in head and neck cancer patients using 3D transformer-based deep learning model.
abstract: Purpose Taste alteration is a common post-treatment side effect of head and neck cancer (HNC) radiotherapy. Accurate normal tissue complication probability (NTCP) models can support treatment planning aimed at reducing side effects that impair quality-of-life. Deep learning (DL) offers opportunities to incorporate full 3D dose, CT, and organofinterest (OOI) data. Using a large prospective cohort, this study explores whether CNN and transformerbased DL models can outperform a conventional logistic regression model for predicting taste alteration 6 months after radiotherapy. Material/methods Data from 972 patients was used, with the endpoint being moderatetosevere patientreported taste alteration at six months (EORTC QLQH&N35). DL models were trained using 3D dose distributions, planning CT, OOI segmentations and clinical features. A conventional NTCP model using oral cavity mean dose, parotid mean dose, and age served as reference. Attention maps were evaluated for the transformer-based DL model to quantify the model attention to specific regions of the head and neck area. In addition, two cropping approaches for the 3D data were compared. Results The CNN and transformer DL models performed comparable to the reference NTCP model in the test set (Reference: AUC = 0.71; ResNet: AUC = 0.68; TransRP: AUC = 0.71), though calibration was best for the reference model. Shifting the crop improved DL performance and transformer attention focused on supraglottic and submandibular regions. Conclusion This study showed that the prediction of taste alteration can be achieved using DL models, particularly transformer-based models which, in contrast to CNNs, can account for global features of comprehensive 3D information of dose distribution, CT-images and organs-of-interest segmentations.

title: Systematic Review of Clinical Utility of Multimodal Imaging in Infectious Posterior Uveitis. Multimodal imaging in Uveitis (MUV) Taskforce Report 12.
abstract: Topic To systematically evaluate the clinical utility of multimodal imaging (MMI) for the diagnosis, activity assessment, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications in the five most prevalent infectious posterior uveitides. Design Systematic review and evidence-based quality appraisal. Participants Original research studies published between January 2018 and September 2025(primary cohort) and 2012-2017(supplemental cohort) evaluating MMI in ocular toxoplasmosis(TOXO), cytomegalovirus retinitis(CMVR), ocular tuberculosis(TB), syphilitic uveitis(SYPH), and acute retinal necrosis(ARN). Methods MEDLINE, Embase, Cochrane, and Scopus were systematically searched. Independent reviewers extracted reported imaging findings and clinical utility statements for: color fundus photography (CFP), fundus autofluorescence (FAF), optical coherence tomography (OCT), fundus fluorescein angiography (FFA), indocyanine green angiography (ICGA), and OCT angiography (OCTA). Methodological quality was assessed using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool (MMAT), and certainty of evidence was graded using a bespoke consensus-based scheme informed by GRADE principles. Main outcome measures (1)reported imaging findings for each entity and modality; and (2)statements of clinical utility for diagnosis, detection of disease activity, longitudinal monitoring, and detection of complications. Results Among 122 included studies (82 primary and 40 supplemental), the primary studies contributed 5,522 individual patient examinations and 574 imaging statements, while the supplemental studies provided corroborating evidence. Overall, 366 clinical utility statements were identified across the four prespecified domains, including 30 statements supporting synergistic MMI strategies. CFP, including studies using ultra-widefield imaging, achieved high certainty for diagnosis and longitudinal monitoring in four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with moderate certainty in ARN. OCT achieved high certainty across all four clinical utility domains for four of five entities (4/5, 80%), with lower certainty in ARN owing to its limited evidence base. FFA achieved high certainty for complication detection in three of five entities. FAF achieved high certainty for disease activity in four of five entities. OCTA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for two of five entities, whereas ICGA achieved high certainty in at least one domain for only one of five entities. Conclusions Substantial evidence exists regarding the imaging findings and clinical utility of MMI in infectious posterior uveitis. Combined MMI enables integrated structural, vascular, and choroidal assessment beyond conventional clinical examination.

title: CBCT-guided plan-of-the-day adaptive radiotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer: Feasibility and dosimetric evaluation in a resource-limited setting.
abstract: Introduction Interfractional anatomical variations during pelvic radiotherapy for locally advanced cervical cancer may compromise target coverage and increase organ-at-risk (OAR) irradiation. This study evaluated the feasibility and dosimetric impact of a cone-beam CT (CBCT)-guided Plan-of-the-Day (PoD) adaptive radiotherapy where resources are limited. Methods Twenty patients treated with definitive chemoradiotherapy were prospectively enrolled. Three volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) plans were generated for each patient using planning target volume margins of 7, 10, and 15 mm around the cervical tumour clinical target volume. Daily CBCT imaging was used to select the most appropriate plan according to daily anatomy. The workflow was implemented using standard CBCT-guided IGRT resources without dedicated online adaptive radiotherapy software. Anatomical variations were assessed over 500 treatment fractions, and dose recalculation was performed on 410 fractions. Results Substantial interfractional anatomical variations were observed. Bladder volume was lower than the planning value in 68.2% of fractions, whereas rectal distension exceeded planning values in 74.4%. The reduced-margin plan was selected in 58.8% of fractions, followed by the standard (27%) and large-margin plans (14.2%). Plan selection was significantly associated with bladder and rectal anatomical variations. Target coverage remained satisfactory across all plans (mean PTV V42.75Gy: 96.8-97.5%), with the predefined V95% criterion achieved in 85.7%, 79.8%, and 89.3% of recalculated fractions for the 7-, 10-, and 15 mm plans, respectively. Larger margins significantly increased bladder and rectal V30Gy and V40Gy values. Conclusion A CBCT-guided PoD strategy was feasible using standard IGRT resources and generally maintained high target coverage despite substantial interfractional anatomical variations. Larger margins increased OAR dose-volume parameters, supporting individualized daily plan selection where dedicated online ART infrastructure is unavailable. Implications for practice CBCT-guided PoD offers a strategy where online adaptive radiotherapy is unavailable.

title: DAG-informed analysis of muscle characteristics and overall survival in patients receiving radical treatment for bladder cancer.
abstract: Background Reduced skeletal muscle (SM) quantity and quality may influence outcomes in bladder cancer, but most studies are associative and vulnerable to confounding and inconsistent covariate adjustment. We applied a directed acyclic graph (DAG)-informed framework to evaluate associations between computed tomography-derived SM characteristics and overall survival (OS) in patients receiving curative-intent radiotherapy-based bladder preservation or radical cystectomy. Methods This retrospective two-centre cohort study included patients treated between 2014 and 2024. Computed tomography imaging closest to definitive local therapy was analysed using an automated segmentation pipeline to quantify SM quantity, expressed as skeletal muscle index (SMI), and quality, expressed as intramuscular adipose tissue ratio (IMATR). A DAG was used to prespecify the adjustment strategy, and Cox models were fitted separately within radiotherapy and surgical cohorts. Results The final cohorts comprised 353 radiotherapy-treated and 117 surgically treated patients. In the radiotherapy cohort, higher SMI was associated with improved OS (HR 0.79, 95% CI 0.66-0.94, p = 0.007), while higher IMATR was associated with worse OS (HR 1.24, 95% CI 1.04-1.48, p = 0.014). In the smaller surgical cohort, point estimates were directionally discordant with the radiotherapy findings and imprecise: SMI HR 1.35 (95% CI 0.99-1.85, p = 0.057) and IMATR HR 0.86 (95% CI 0.62-1.21, p = 0.39). Conclusions In this DAG-informed analysis, higher SMI and lower IMATR were associated with improved OS in radiotherapy-treated patients. Surgical estimates were imprecise and should be considered exploratory. These findings are hypothesis-generating and support further evaluation of CT-derived muscle characteristics as prognostic markers within radiotherapy-treated populations but cannot yet establish a differential benefit for radiotherapy vs cystectomy.

title: Carcinomatous meningitis: Current insights into diagnosis, prognosis and management.
abstract: Carcinomatous meningitis, or leptomeningeal metastasis, is a severe neurological complication of solid and haematological malignancies caused by dissemination of tumour cells within the leptomeninges and cerebrospinal fluid pathways. Clinical presentation is heterogeneous, including headache, intracranial hypertension, cranial nerve palsies or radiculopathy, which frequently leads to diagnostic delay. Diagnosis relies on converging clinical, radiological, and cerebrospinal fluid findings, with gadolinium-enhanced magnetic resonance imaging of the brain and spine and cerebrospinal fluid cytology remaining central despite imperfect sensitivity. Emerging tools, particularly cerebrospinal fluid circulating tumour cells and circulating tumour DNA, may improve early detection and molecular characterisation. Prognosis remains poor, with survival usually measured in months. Management should be individualised according to performance status, tumour subtype, and systemic disease control, and may combine symptomatic measures, radiotherapy, targeted systemic therapies, and, in selected patients, intrathecal chemotherapy. Early integration of palliative care remains a key component of management.

title: Artificial intelligence in diabetic retinopathy: From deep learning to foundation models, clinical translation, and real-world deployment.
abstract: Diabetic retinopathy (DR) remains a leading cause of preventable vision impairment worldwide, with its burden increasing in parallel with the global diabetes pandemic. As a progressive microvascular disorder with neurovascular unit involvement, DR is driven by retinal ischemia, inflammation, and pathological neovascularization, while diabetic macular edema (DME) continues to represent a principal cause of vision loss. This structured narrative review provides a critical synthesis of advances in diabetic retinopathy diagnosis, retinal imaging, treatment strategies, and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled screening published from January 2020 through March 2026, while selectively incorporating earlier landmark studies to provide clinical and methodological context. We summarize contemporary screening pathways and emerging retinal imaging modalities, including ultra-widefield photography (up to ~200° field of view), optical coherence tomography (OCT), and OCT angiography, examining how complementary structural and vascular biomarkers are reshaping disease severity assessment and DME characterization. We then review the evolution of AI methodologies, highlighting a transition from task-specific convolutional neural network pipelines toward transformer-based and self-supervised representation learning, including retina-specific foundation models designed to reduce annotation burden and improve robustness and generalizability under domain shift. Beyond algorithmic performance on curated benchmarks, we emphasize key translational requirements for clinical adoption, including model calibration, uncertainty-aware triage, image quality control, and external validation across imaging devices and diverse populations. Recent prospective and implementation studies across diverse healthcare systems demonstrate that the real-world effectiveness of AI-enabled DR screening depends not only on diagnostic accuracy but also on image gradability, clinically appropriate operating thresholds, uncertainty management, external validation, referral capacity, and integration with established care pathways. Evidence from the Asia-Pacific region provides important examples of these implementation challenges in heterogeneous and resource-constrained screening environments. Specific attention is given to the identification and mitigation strategies for fundus pigmentation-related performance disparities and the governance of autonomous versus hybrid human-AI screening models within evolving regulatory frameworks. Finally, we examine emerging work in oculomics for systemic risk stratification and propose a pragmatic clinical readiness framework centered on validation hierarchy, safety monitoring, and workflow integration. Particular emphasis is placed on the translational readiness of foundation models, multimodal retinal intelligence, and emerging technologies for large-scale screening, therapeutic decision-making, and longitudinal disease monitoring.

title: Peripheral exudative hemorrhagic chorioretinopathy: A comprehensive review of clinical features, differential diagnosis, pathogenesis-related disease spectra, and management.
abstract: Peripheral exudative hemorrhagic chorioretinopathy (PEHCR) is a peripheral chorioretinopathy characterized by retinal pigment epithelium detachment with either blood, exudation, or both, and may present with macular hemorrhage, macular exudation, and vitreous hemorrhage. PEHCR exhibits a variety of features on fundus fluorescein angiography, indocyanine green angiography, and ultrasound examinations. The hemorrhagic type PEHCR may greatly resemble malignant melanoma, whereas the exudative type can mimics primary vitreoretinal lymphoma making differential diagnosis of great importance. The pathogenesis may involve choroidal neovascularization. Early studies suggested a link to age-related macular degeneration, while subsequent research has revealed a close association with polypoidal choroidal vasculopathy and pachychoroid disease spectrum. Most cases of PEHCR are self-limiting and may be observed alone. For those complicated by, or at risk of, macular exudation, macular hemorrhage, as well as vitreous hemorrhage, management strategies include intravitreal anti-vascular endothelial growth factor injections, vitrectomy, laser photocoagulation, photodynamic therapy, and cryotherapy.

title: Integrative single-cell and computational pathology analyses reveal a C11orf24-associated stem-like epithelial population linked to tumor microenvironment remodeling and immune evasion in bladder cancer.
abstract: Background Cancer stem-like cells drive tumor progression and therapeutic resistance, yet the epithelial stemness hierarchy in bladder cancer (BLCA) remains poorly defined. We aimed to characterize stemness-associated epithelial populations and their clinical significance. Methods We analyzed single-cell RNA sequencing data from 92,218 cells across 13 treatment-naïve BLCA samples to characterize epithelial stemness and tumor-microenvironment interactions. Spatial transcriptomics and independent bulk cohorts were used for orthogonal and clinical validation. An HStem-associated histopathology-based prognostic model was developed by integrating quantitative image features with deep-learning representations, followed by functional validation of the candidate gene C11orf24. Results We identified a highly stem-like epithelial population (HStem) at the apex of the differentiation hierarchy, exhibiting MYC activation, oxidative phosphorylation, and DNA repair enrichment, with preferential presence in advanced-stage tumors. HStem cells were inferred to serve as major communication hubs within the TME, interacting extensively with fibroblasts and endothelial cells via MIF-CD74/CXCR4 and MIF-CD74/CD44 axes. An 86-gene HStem signature enabled development of a robust image-based prognostic model. High-risk tumors showed immune exclusion, immunosuppressive enrichment, T-cell dysfunction, and predicted checkpoint blockade resistance. C11orf24 emerged as a candidate stemness-associated regulator; C11orf24-positive cells displayed enhanced stemness and stromal interactions. Functional experiments demonstrated that C11orf24 perturbation altered clonogenic growth, migration, and invasion in BLCA cells. Pharmacogenomic analyses identified predicted therapeutic vulnerabilities that warrant experimental validation. Conclusions We identify an HStem population associated with BLCA progression, microenvironmental remodeling, and immune evasion. Integrating single-cell and spatial transcriptomics with computational pathology, we establish a clinically relevant stemness framework and identify C11orf24 as a potential therapeutic target, offering opportunities for stemness-directed precision oncology.

title: Research Progress of Low-Intensity Pulsed Ultrasound in Parkinson's Disease.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder where current pharmacological and surgical interventions, including Deep Brain Stimulation, often fail to reverse neuronal degeneration or halt disease progression. Low-intensity pulsed ultrasound (LIPUS) has emerged as a novel, non-invasive neuromodulation technology with significant therapeutic potential. This review synthesizes current research on the key acoustic parameters, biological mechanisms, and clinical applications of LIPUS in PD. Unlike High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound (HIFU), which relies on thermal ablation to destroy target nuclei (e.g., Vim, STN), LIPUS utilizes low-energy mechanical waves (typically <3 W/cm²) to exert non-thermal regulatory effects without damaging tissue. Mechanisms of action include the modulation of mechanosensitive ion channels (e.g., Piezo1), enhancement of neuroplasticity via brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF), promotion of autophagy, and regulation of microglial phenotypes to reduce neuroinflammation. We further compare LIPUS with HIFU, highlighting the superiority of LIPUS regarding safety, reversibility, and the absence of requirement for MRI-based thermal monitoring. While preliminary clinical studies using wearable LIPUS devices indicate improvements in motor and cognitive functions, a unified consensus on optimal stimulation parameters and targeting strategies is lacking. Future research should focus on large-scale, standardized clinical trials to establish precise protocols for LIPUS as a disease-modifying therapy for PD.

title: ADHD symptom positivity and its association with medication adherence and psychiatric burden in adults with epilepsy.
abstract: Background Attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) symptoms are increasingly recognized in adults with epilepsy (AwE) and may contribute to psychiatric burden, seizure-related outcomes, and treatment adherence. We therefore investigated the frequency of ADHD symptom positivity and its associations with medication adherence, psychiatric symptoms, seizure burden, and neurophysiological findings. Methods This cross-sectional study included 100 AwE and 94 healthy controls. ADHD symptoms were assessed using the Adult ADHD Self-Report Scale (ASRS-v1.1). Anxiety and depressive symptoms were evaluated using the Beck Anxiety Inventory and Beck Depression Inventory, respectively. Medication adherence was assessed using the Morisky Medication Adherence Scale (MMAS-8). Participants were classifiedas ASRS-positive or ASRS-negative according to the six-item ASRS Part A screener. Clinical, psychiatric, electroencephalographic, and magnetic resonance imaging findings were compared between groups. Multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with ADHD-symptom-positivity. Results ADHD-symptom-positivity was significantly more frequent in AwE than in healthy controls (50.0% vs. 25.5%, p = 0.001). Within the epilepsy cohort, ASRS-positive participants demonstrated lower medication adherence (p = 0.010), higher rates of poor adherence (70.0% vs. 48.0%, p = 0.042), higher anxiety (p = 0.002), and depression scores (p < 0.001). Clinically significant anxiety and depression were also more common among ASRS-positive participants (p = 0.027 and p < 0.001, respectively). In multivariable analysis, depression score was independently associated with ADHD-symptom-positivity (OR = 1.147, 95% CI 1.039-1.267, p = 0.007). Conclusions ADHD-symptom-positivity is common in AwE and is associated with poorer medication adherence in the between-group analysis, but this association did not remain statistically significant after multivariable adjustment, while greater psychiatric symptom burden was observed. Routine screening for ADHD-related symptoms may facilitate identification of adults with epilepsy at increased riskfor adverse clinical outcomes and support more comprehensive epilepsy care.

title: Multimodal precision diagnostics in clinical xenotransplantation.
abstract: Recent breakthroughs in pig-to-human xenotransplantation have successfully prevented hyperacute rejection of kidney, heart, liver and lung xenografts, marking a milestone long considered a critical barrier. However, these major advances also brought new challenges into focus, as immune-mediated graft injuries including antibody-mediated rejection, T cell-mediated rejection and innate immune activation have been observed in most xenotransplantation procedures to date. Detection and management of these injuries remain a critical bottleneck, as conventional histopathology and standard clinical monitoring lack the sensitivity required to identify subclinical injury early enough to guide timely intervention. This diagnostic gap underscores an urgent need for the development of advanced, multimodal precision diagnostic frameworks to enhance immune surveillance, which will be essential for standardizing clinical protocols and enabling pathogenesis-driven therapeutic intervention. This approach will inform both immunosuppressive regimens and future gene editing strategies aimed at engineering rejection-resistant porcine organs, ultimately prolonging graft survival. Broad adoption of such an integrative strategy will be essential to transition xenotransplantation from an experimental intervention into a safe, scalable and patient-centred clinical therapy. In this Review, we synthesize recent progress in xenotransplantation and position multimodal precision diagnostics as a pivotal strategy to address the remaining immunological and clinical barriers to widespread clinical implementation.

title: Carbon nanotube-induced magnetic shielding effects on <sup>129</sup>Xe NMR from equivariant neural networks.
abstract: Equivariant graph neural networks (EGNNs) have been successfully used in building efficient and accurate machine learning interatomic potentials (MLIPs) for molecular dynamics (MD) and to predict nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) parameters in complex systems. In this work, EGNNs are used to fine-tune an atomistic foundation model, which serves as an MLIP for large-scale molecular dynamics simulations of xenon in carbon nanotubes. In addition, EGNNs are employed to develop a machine-learning model for the 129 Xe NMR magnetic shielding tensor, σ , enabling its direct prediction from the MLMD snapshots. Both models are data-efficient and remain accurate well beyond their training data. Using this dual-model framework, we show that xenon encapsulated in carbon nanotubes experiences a nanotube-induced, negative 129 Xe isotropic chemical shift that varies non-monotonically with nanotube diameter and depends further on temperature and Xe loading, establishing this dual-model approach as an efficient route to interpret confinement-driven 129 Xe NMR response.

title: Comparative Assessment of Orofacial Myofunction, Strength, and Quality of Life in Children With and Without Anterior Open Bite: The OMBIT Study.
abstract: Purpose Anterior open bite (AOB) is a multifactorial malocclusion frequently associated with nonnutritive sucking habits (NNSHs) and orofacial dysfunctions. However, little is known about the specific orofacial strength and endurance profile in affected children. This study evaluated myofunctional history, orofacial myofunctional status, orofacial strength, and oral health-related quality of life (OHRQoL) in children in the mixed dentition stage with AOB, compared to controls without AOB. Method Sixteen children with AOB in the mixed dentition stage ( M age = 8.2 years) and 16 age- and gender-matched controls participated in this cross-sectional study. Dental and orofacial histories were collected through parental questionnaires. Palatal and occlusal morphologies were assessed using intraoral scans. Orofacial function was examined using the Orofacial Myofunctional Evaluation with Scores (OMES) protocol and ultrasound imaging. Maximum isometric pressure and endurance of the tongue and lips were measured using the Iowa Oral Performance Instrument (IOPI). OHRQoL was assessed using the Child Oral Health Impact Profile-Ortho (COHIP-Ortho). Results Oral habits (e.g., nail biting, lip licking) were more frequently observed in the AOB group, and parental reports indicated that persistent open mouth behavior was reported more often in children with AOB. Two thirds of the participants had a history of NNSH, with similar prevalence across groups; however, AOB was associated with NNSH cessation at an older age. AOB was associated with higher anterior tongue endurance. No other significant differences were found in tongue or lip strength or endurance, OMES scores, or COHIP-Ortho scores. Conclusions The absence of group differences in orofacial strength and most endurance measures suggests that, in this sample, mixed-dentition AOB was not accompanied by generalized orofacial strength deficits. These findings support early functional screening and suggest that function-focused orofacial myofunctional therapy, rather than strength-based training, may be a relevant approach in children with AOB.

title: Ultrasound in fetal growth restriction.
abstract: Abstract Fetal growth restriction (FGR) is associated with increased perinatal morbidity and mortality. Its recognition requires differentiation from a constitutionally small-for-gestational-age (SGA) fetus. Based on the current AWMF S2k guideline, this CME review summarizes the ultrasound assessment and clinical management of suspected FGR. Accurate first-trimester dating, standardized fetal biometry, assessment of amniotic fluid volume, and detailed anatomical evaluation form the basis of diagnosis. Consensus-based criteria distinguish early FGR before 32 + 0 weeks' gestation from late FGR at or beyond 32 + 0 weeks' gestation. Multivessel Doppler assessment of the umbilical artery, middle cerebral artery, cerebroplacental ratio, and ductus venosus provides complementary information on placental resistance, fetal redistribution, and cardiovascular decompensation. Cardiotocography, including computerized analysis of short-term variation in early FGR, is used as part of multimodal surveillance and should not be interpreted in isolation. The review discusses appropriate monitoring intervals, indications for inpatient care, antenatal corticosteroids and fetal neuroprotection when preterm birth is anticipated, as well as gestational-age- and finding-dependent timing and mode of delivery. A practical clinical case illustrates the diagnostic pathway from abnormal fetal biometry to delivery planning.

title: Temporal trends in incidence, clinical characteristics and outcomes of pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis in Southern Denmark from 2009 to 2022: a retrospective population-based cohort study.
abstract: Objectives Pyogenic vertebral osteomyelitis (PVO) is a severe infection with increasing incidence. We aimed to describe long-term population-based temporal trends in incidence, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, microbiology, and outcomes. Materials and methods We conducted a retrospective population-based cohort study including 1,017 adults with multidisciplinary team-verified PVO diagnosed at a tertiary infectious diseases referral centre in the Region of Southern Denmark between 2009 and 2022. Incidence rates (IRs) per 100,000 person-years (PY) were calculated using regional population data and compared across three calendar periods (2009-2013, 2014-2018, 2019-2022). Temporal changes in clinical characteristics, microbiology, diagnostic strategies, and outcomes were assessed. Results In total, 1,017 patients were included. The crude IR increased from 4.7 per 100,000 PY in 2009-2013 to 11.0 in 2019-2022, with the largest increase among patients aged ≥70 years. Mean age and comorbidity burden rose over time. Pain was common, fever was often absent, and neurological deficits occurred in 33.5% ( n = 341). Postsurgical infection was the most frequent primary focus, and concomitant endocarditis occurred in 8.3% ( n = 84). A microbiological diagnosis was established in 64.8% ( n = 635) of cases, most commonly Staphylococcus aureus . Use of Fluorine-18 Fluorodeoxyglucose Positron Emission Tomography/Computed Tomography ([ 18 F]FDG-PET/CT) increased over time. Median hospital stay remained 33 days. One-year mortality increased from 9.5% to 18.2%, while relapse declined, resulting in a stable composite risk of death or relapse (20.7%). Conclusions The incidence of PVO increased markedly from 2009 to 2022, predominantly in older patients with comorbidities. Despite improved diagnostics, microbiologically-negative cases remain frequent. Mortality remained high and increased over time.

In total, 1,017 patients were included. The crude IR increased from 4.7 per 100,000 PY in 2009-2013 to 11.0 in 2019-2022, with the largest increase among patients aged ≥70 years. title: Clinical features associated with HFUS-defined vascular occlusion after hyaluronic acid facial injections: a retrospective exploratory study.
abstract: Hyaluronic acid (HA) filler injections are widely used in aesthetic treatments but can cause vascular occlusion. Early diagnosis is often delayed due to reliance on clinical experience. High-frequency ultrasound (HFUS) offers a noninvasive diagnostic method. The study aims to explore the association between clinical warning signs and HFUS-defined vascular occlusion after HA filler injections. This retrospective study analyzed 57 patients with suspected vascular occlusion after HA filler injections. HFUS and a clinical scoring system covering seven symptom categories were used for early evaluation. Occlusion and non-occlusion groups were compared using HFUS and clinical scores. Among 57 clinically suspected cases, 42 (73.7%) were classified as HFUS-defined vascular occlusion and 15 (26.3%) were classified as non-occlusion. In multivariable analysis, skin color change (OR 30.390, 95% CI: 2.482-372.039; p = .008) and delayed capillary refill time (OR 185.936, 95% CI: 2.638- 13,095.200; p = .016) were associated factors of vascular occlusion. A two-variable model incorporating there two features yielded an AUC of 0.944 (95% CI: 0.891-0.998). Skin color change and delayed capillary refill time were associated with HFUS-defined vascular occlusion in this exploratory cohort. These findings may help inform clinical assessment but require prospective validation in independent populations.

title: AnF-DiffPET: anatomy- and frequency-guided diffusion for simulated low-dose PET/CT denoising.
abstract: Objective. Positron emission tomography (PET) provides essential functional information for disease assessment. However, reducing injected activity or acquisition time produces low-dose (LD) PET with stronger count-dependent noise and less reliable uptake quantification. Diffusion models offer a promising solution for PET denoising by progressively recovering high-dose (HD) PET images from LD inputs. However, LD-to-HD PET denoising remains challenging because of limited anatomical guidance, unstable multi-scale feature propagation, and inaccurate recovery of uptake patterns in the frequency domain. Approach. We propose AnF-DiffPET, an anatomy- and frequency-guided diffusion framework for computed tomography (CT)-conditioned LD PET denoising. The framework integrates anatomical-frequency guidance, Multi-Scale Cross-Transformer Reconstruction, and Frequency-Contrastive Hard Mining to enhance anatomy-aware feature modulation and frequency-domain consistency during denoising. Main results. Experimental results across four simulated LD PET/CT datasets show that the proposed method improves image fidelity, anatomical consistency, and quantitative fidelity over representative CNN-based, GAN-based, Transformer-based, Mamba-based, and diffusion-based methods. Significance. AnF-DiffPET provides a PET/CT-specific diffusion restoration framework that combines anatomical guidance, multi-scale feature reconstruction, and frequency-domain regularization for LD PET denoising. The code and trained models will be publicly released upon acceptance.

title: Self-Supervised, Physics-Driven Sparse-Array XACT Reconstruction Using Sinusoidal Implicit Neural Representation.
abstract: X-ray induced acoustic computed tomography (XACT) enables high-contrast bone imaging but typically relies on dense and expensive transducer arrays. Sparse array sampling introduces severe streak artifacts and loss of fine structural details in conventional reconstruction. This work aims to establish a robust reconstruction framework that achieves high-fidelity structural imaging under sparse sampling, thereby overcoming hardware density limitations and facilitating low-cost, high-resolution skeletal health assessment. We propose a self-supervised, physics-driven framework based on sinusoidal implicit neural representation. The unknown initial pressure distribution is parameterized as a continuous coordinate-to-pressure function via a sinusoidal representation network, and is coupled end-to-end with a differentiable acoustic forward simulator implemented in j‑Wave. Network optimization is performed by minimizing waveform residuals between measured and predicted signals, eliminating the need for paired ground-truth data. To improve training stability and accelerate convergence, an adjoint-based warm start and total variation regularization are employed. In experiments on simulated hand and femoral bone sparse array datasets, the proposed method consistently outperforms conventional approaches under various sparse sampling conditions. Notably, for an osteoporotic femur imaged with only 64 transducer elements, the method effectively suppresses artifacts and faithfully preserves fine trabecular structures, achieving a peak signal-to-noise ratio of 32.43 dB and a root mean square error of 0.0239, surpassing the structural and quantitative accuracy of traditional reconstruction using a full 256‑element array. These results demonstrate that the framework supports stable XACT reconstruction under sparse array conditions and, with its favorable artifact suppression and microstructural preservation capabilities, offers a practical computational pathway toward low-cost, high-quality XACT imaging.

title: A transparent gel pad bolus enabling direct skin recognition in surface-guided radiation therapy.
abstract: Objectives To evaluate the feasibility of repurposing a transparent ultrasound gel pad as a radiotherapy bolus, we focused on dosimetric performance and compatibility with surface-guided radiation therapy (SGRT). Methods A gel pad bolus composed of tamarind seed gum and polyhydric alcohols was compared with a conventional gel bolus and a thermoplastic bolus. Percent depth dose was measured for 6 MV and 10 MV photon beams and 6 MeV and 9 MeV electron beams. Straight-line optical transmittance was assessed over 380-830 nm. Surface recognition accuracy was quantified using the AlignRT SGRT system on a breast phantom. Results The gel pad produced a measurable bolus effect for both photon and electron beams, although superficial dose enhancement was lower than that of conventional materials (85.5% vs 90.3-91.5% at 6 MV). Deep doses beyond dmax agreed within 1% for photon beams. At 730 nm, the gel pad bolus demonstrated high transmittance (92.3%), compared with the gel (19.8%) and HM (36.6%) boluses. The SGRT recognition rate with the gel pad bolus (89.10%) was comparable to the no-bolus condition (92.93%, p = 0.13), whereas conventional boluses significantly reduced recognition (p < 0.001). Conclusions The transparent gel pad bolus enabled direct SGRT-based recognition of the underlying skin surface while maintaining clinically relevant bolus functionality. Advances in knowledge Optical transparency enables SGRT monitoring through a bolus, highlighting optical compatibility as an important design consideration.

title: Regional blood-brain barrier dysfunction maps to lower performance in cognitive ageing.
abstract: Age-related cognitive decline is a common and growing public health challenge, associated with loss of independence, reduced quality of life, increased caregiver burden and substantial healthcare and societal costs. Yet cognitive decline in ageing is heterogeneous, and current clinical constructs do not reliably capture the underlying biological mechanisms or predict progression to dementia. This cross-sectional study examined whether blood-brain barrier dysfunction (BBBD) provides a biologically supported correlate of cognitive performance beyond clinical diagnosis. The study included 46 patients with mild cognitive impairment (MCI), 46 age-matched controls and 43 young controls. BBBD was assessed using dynamic contrast-enhanced MRI in 42 patients with MCI and all controls, alongside volumetric brain analysis. Standardized NeuroTrax cognitive assessment data were analysed for 41 MCI patients and 19 age-matched controls. BBBD was analysed using the BBBdetect software (Emagix Inc, Nova Scotia, Canada), quantifying voxelwise and region-wise blood-brain barrier permeability; volumetric analysis was performed using the Volbrain software; and cognitive performance was stratified into low- and high-performance subgroups based on modified z-scores. Compared with young controls, the older cohort (MCI patients combined with age-matched controls) showed significantly greater BBBD volume and regional extent. Permeability increased with age and showed marked inter-individual variability. Across participants, lower cognitive performance was associated with a greater number of regions exhibiting BBBD. Receiver operating characteristic analysis identified domain-specific spatial patterns of BBBD linked to poor performance in memory, executive, attention, verbal and motor domains, implicating frontal, cingulate, hippocampal, basal ganglia and cerebellar regions. In contrast, volumetric analyses revealed expected age-related reductions in grey and white matter and cortical thickness along with increased ventricular volume; however, these structural changes showed weak to no associations with cognitive performance. These findings suggest that BBBD is widespread in ageing and that regional BBBD maps to domain-specific cognitive deficits. BBBD thus emerges as a biologically relevant biomarker of age-related cognitive impairment and a potential therapeutic target for preserving cognitive function in ageing.

title: Endoscopic and histologic healing distribution and persistent rectosigmoiditis in moderate-to-severe ulcerative colitis.
abstract: Background Mucosal healing in ulcerative colitis (UC) is believed to follow a proximal-to-distal pattern. We evaluated colonic healing distribution in patients with moderate-to-severe UC receiving adalimumab. Methods Patients from the SERENE UC (Study of a Novel Approach to Induction and Maintenance Dosing with Adalimumab in Patients with Moderate to Severe Ulcerative Colitis) trial with full colonoscopies and segmental biopsies at screening, weeks 8, and 52 were included for endoscopic and histologic analyses if baseline Mayo endoscopic subscore (MES) or Robarts Histopathology Index (RHI) score, respectively, was >0 in the ascending, transverse, and/or descending colon. Data were analyzed using a mixed model for repeated measures to account for clustering of segments within a patient. Results Endoscopic and histologic analyses comprised 76 and 79 patients, respectively. Score reductions were significantly greater vs the rectum in the ascending (week 8: MES, mean -0.78 [95% confidence interval (CI), -1.03 to -0.52]; RHI, mean -4.70 [95% CI, -6.92 to -2.49]; week 52: MES, mean -0.63 [95% CI, -0.91 to -0.35]; RHI, mean -2.39 [95% CI, -4.64 to -0.15]), transverse (week 8: MES, mean -0.69 [95% CI, -0.94 to -0.43]; RHI, mean -3.57 [95% CI, -5.62 to -1.51]; week 52: MES, mean -0.64 [95% CI, -0.89 to -0.38]; RHI, mean -2.88 [95% CI, -4.99 to -0.77]), and descending colon (week 8: MES, mean -0.40 [95% CI, -0.67 to -0.13]; RHI, mean -2.55 [95% CI, -4.94 to -0.16]; week 52: MES, mean -0.52 [95% CI, -0.70 to -0.34]; RHI, mean -3.47 [95% CI, -5.37 to -1.56]). Endoscopic improvement/remission and histologic remission were significantly more likely in the ascending and transverse colon than the rectum. Conclusions Our findings demonstrate that endoscopic and histologic healing is more challenging in the rectum compared with proximal colonic segments.

title: Benchmark Evaluation of Vision-Enabled Large Language Models in Mammography: A Case-Control Study.
abstract: Objective To compare the diagnostic performance of five contemporary vision-enabled large language models (LLMs) in mammography interpretation using a case-control benchmark design. Methods A total of 200 cases were analyzed using a quota-balanced case-control design (100 malignant, BI-RADS 4-5; 100 controls, BI-RADS 1-2). All models (ChatGPT-5T, ChatGPT-5I, ChatGPT-4o, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Gemini 2.5 Flash) received standard mammography images. Models were evaluated for lesion detection, laterality, quadrant localization, lesion type, and malignant-benign discrimination. Performance was assessed using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, Cohen's κ, and area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC). Breast density was recorded for all cases, while histopathological subtype and lesion size were documented for malignant cases. Results Lesion detection accuracy ranged from 79% to 91%, with high malignant sensitivity (92%-100%) but lower specificity in normal cases (24%-82%). ChatGPT-5T performed best in laterality (83%; κ = 0.70) and quadrant localization (73%; κ = 0.62). Lesion type classification was modest (74%-85%). In malignant-benign discrimination, ChatGPT-5T achieved the highest balanced accuracy (87%), while ChatGPT-4o showed poor specificity (28%). The study cohort was predominantly composed of lower-density breasts, larger lesions, and invasive ductal carcinoma as the most common subtype. Conclusion Vision-enabled LLMs demonstrated high sensitivity for breast lesion detection and classification tasks. More deliberative models, particularly ChatGPT-5T, consistently outperformed faster counterparts, especially in spatial reasoning tasks. However, reduced specificity in normal cases underscores that current LLM outputs should remain under radiologist supervision as supportive second-reader tools rather than standalone diagnostic systems. Given the quota-balanced design and cohort composition, results should be interpreted as comparative benchmarking rather than real-world diagnostic performance.

title: Foundation models for cancer: advancing diagnosis, prognosis, and treatment response-an NCI workshop report.
abstract: From March 24-26, 2026, the National Cancer Institute convened the Foundation Models for Cancer Workshop, bringing together more than thirty speakers from academia, government, and industry and attracting more than 2,000 registrants worldwide. The workshop examined the current state and future potential of foundation models and related artificial intelligence (AI) technologies in oncology. Presentations spanned single-cell biology, computational pathology, medical imaging, electronic health records, drug discovery, federated learning, and clinical decision support. Several themes emerged across the three-day meeting. First, the development of robust foundation models depends on access to high-quality, multimodal cancer datasets that are representative of the patient populations, disease stages, and clinical settings encountered in routine care. Second, prospective validation and evaluation in real-world clinical environments are essential for establishing the reliability, generalizability, and utility of AI-enabled tools. Third, while technical advances continue at a rapid pace, successful translation into cancer research and patient care will also require attention to implementation, workflow integration, interpretability, and data governance. Collectively, the workshop highlighted both the opportunities and challenges associated with applying foundation models to cancer research and clinical care and provided a forum for discussing future directions for the field.

title: The Ongoing Utility of Historical Military Photofluorographs-Tools to Identify Fallen US Soldiers From Past Wars as Cross-Validated by DNA and Dental Data in 180 Cases.
abstract: Introduction Mass chest X-ray formed a routine part of induction processes to the US armed forces in the 1940-1950s for tuberculosis screening. Today, the skeletal structure recorded in these medical miniature films serves to identify these same soldiers. In the US military's accounting/repatriation setting, chest radiograph comparisons have grown to be a primary identification mechanism alongside DNA and dental records. Identifications are now routinely conducted with contributions from miniature radiographic films. This article reviews the miniature radiographic film as an identification tool and provides the first evaluation of findings (180 cases) against gold standards of DNA and dental analyses for the very same cases. Materials and methods This article reviews both miniature film photofluorographs and the standardized chest radiograph comparison (CXR) protocol employed by the Defense POW/MIA Accounting Agency (DPAA) for identification. Additionally, all DPAA cases (2010-2025) where radiographic CXR resulted in a match result (280) were reviewed for additional DNA and/or dental record findings, providing 180 cases where dual-modality result existed to cross-validation test the radiographic analyses. Results For 172 DNA cases, there was no instance of disagreement between the chest radiograph result and the independently acquired Armed Forces DNA Identification Laboratory's DNA result. For 8 dental cases reporting a positive match result, the CXR identity finding was identical (both evidence lines identified the same person). To be conservative, we assume that the next future CXR case to be conducted using miniature films will yield an erroneous result, thereby setting a positive predictive value for radiographic comparison of 99.4% (=180 correct results/181 total decisions). Conclusions Miniature chest radiographs provide useful identification-relevant information. DPAA casework provides a rare circumstance to evaluate the accuracy of miniature film radiograph comparisons across a large sample, as multiple independent and parallel lines of analysis exist for single cases. Evaluation of these cases (180 in total) reveals that the military miniature films supply the same name associations that DNA and forensic odontology provide. The positive predictive value is high (99.4%), conservatively assuming the next case to be an incorrect one. This confirms the value of the miniature chest film and CXR methods, when DNA and dental records alone are unable to provide definitive answers.

title: Diagnostic Performance of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema Score for Acute Respiratory Distress Syndrome-Post Hoc Analysis of the "Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis" Study.
abstract: Objectives To determine the diagnostic accuracy of the Radiographic Assessment of Lung Edema (RALE) score for acute respiratory distress syndrome (ARDS) and its interobserver reliability. Design Post hoc analysis of a prospective observational cohort study. Setting ICUs at Vanderbilt University Medical Center participating in the Validating Acute Lung Injury Biomarkers for Diagnosis study. Patients Adult patients receiving invasive ventilation for at least two consecutive days, with chest radiographs available on the first 2 ICU days. Interventions None. Measurements and main results Chest radiographs from the first 2 ICU days were scored independently by at least two experienced raters; scores were averaged per radiograph, and the highest averaged score from ICU day 1 or 2 was selected for analysis. The primary outcome was ARDS according to the Berlin definition during the first 2 ICU days. Of 236 patients, 92 (39%) had ARDS. The median RALE score was higher in patients with ARDS than in those without (29.5 [22.2-34.5] vs. 12.2 [7.5-17.8]; p < 0.01). The area under the receiver operating characteristic curve was 0.93 (95% CI, 0.90-0.96). At the optimal cutoff of 20, sensitivity was 85%, specificity 83%, positive predictive value 76%, and negative predictive value 90%. Interobserver reliability was high, with pairwise intraclass correlation coefficients ranging from 0.81 to 0.87. Conclusions In patients invasively ventilated for at least 2 days, the RALE score demonstrated excellent diagnostic accuracy for ARDS at a cutoff of 20, together with high interobserver reliability, supporting its potential role as a standardized radiographic tool in the diagnosis of ARDS.

title: What Is the Validity of Traction MR Arthrography for Detecting Lesions of the Ligamentous-Fossa-Foveolar Complex in Patients Undergoing Joint-preserving Surgery Through Surgical Hip Dislocation?
abstract: Background Accurate preoperative characterization of intraarticular abnormalities is important when planning hip-preserving surgery in young, active patients. Lesions of the ligamentum teres and the associated acetabular fossa and fovea capitis (forming the ligamentous-fossa-foveolar complex [LFFC]) are frequently observed intraoperatively, although their relationship with hip pain in patients without osteoarthritis remains uncertain. These lesions have received limited attention in preoperative imaging. Questions/purposes (1) What is the intraobserver and interobserver reliability of traction MR arthrography for assessing lesions of the LFFC? (2) What is the diagnostic performance of traction MR arthrography for detecting these lesions compared with intraoperative findings at surgical hip dislocation? Methods Between April 2019 and April 2022, we retrospectively identified 214 hips from a consecutive cohort of patients undergoing surgical hip dislocation at a single tertiary hip preservation center. We performed this surgery for a variety of indications, including for symptomatic femoroacetabular impingement, childhood hip diseases, and for surgically treating acetabular fractures. During this period, preoperative MR arthrography was part of the routine preoperative work-up in all patients for assessment of intraarticular abnormalities, planning for intraoperative instrument and graft needs, and prognostic purposes. MR arthrography results were not considered when choosing surgical approach. Patients without traction MR arthrography were excluded. A total of 70 patients were available for final analysis. Traction MR arthrography served as the index test and intraoperative assessment during surgical hip dislocation as the reference gold standard. The decision to perform surgical hip dislocation was based on the clinical and standard radiographic evaluation and generally not influenced by traction MR arthrography findings. Six observers (three board-certified orthopaedic surgeons with expertise in hip-preserving surgery and three board-certified radiologists with specific expertise in musculoskeletal imaging) independently conducted measurements twice using an adapted version of a previously validated grading system (grade 0, normal; grade I, degeneration; grade II, partial defect; grade III, complete defect); for diagnostic performance, findings were dichotomized as lesion absent (grade 0) or present (grade > 0). Intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) with 95% confidence interval (CI) were calculated to assess intraobserver reliability and interobserver reproducibility of the adapted grading system. The diagnostic performance of traction MR arthrography for detecting lesions of the LFFC using intraoperative findings as a gold standard was determined by calculating sensitivity, specificity, positive and negative predictive values, accuracy, and positive and negative likelihood ratios. Results Intraobserver reliability ICCs ranged from 0.54 to 0.69 for ligamentum teres lesions, 0.21 to 0.64 for fossa lesions, and 0.30 to 0.64 for fovea lesions. Interobserver reproducibility ranged from 0.71 to 0.84 for fossa lesions, 0.73 to 0.77 for fovea lesions, and 0.78 to 0.79 for ligamentum teres lesions. Traction MR arthrography demonstrated limited diagnostic performance for lesion detection. The sensitivity was 86% for ligamentum teres lesions, 79% for fossa lesions, and 75% for fovea lesions, whereas specificity was low at 32%, 52%, and 50%, respectively. Overall accuracy ranged from 54% to 67%. Conclusion In this cohort of patients undergoing surgical hip dislocation, contrast-enhanced traction MR arthrography demonstrated limited ability to detect and grade lesions of the LFFC preoperatively. Future prospective studies using standardized imaging protocols are needed to determine whether diagnostic performance can be improved. Level of evidence Level III, diagnostic study.

title: Group A Streptococcus in an Unexpected Site: Temporal Pyomyositis in 2 Children.
abstract: Background Pyomyositis is an uncommon bacterial infection of skeletal muscle. Group A Streptococcus (GAS) accounts for a smaller proportion of pediatric cases, and temporal muscle involvement is exceptionally rare. Case description We report 2 previously healthy children, a 7-year-old boy and a 6-year-old girl, who presented with acute otitis media (AOM) and painful unilateral temporomandibular swelling. Computed tomography revealed AOM with temporal myositis, complicated by mastoiditis in the first case. Both were treated with intravenous antibiotics, and the first case required drainage and mastoidectomy, with full recovery. GAS was isolated in both cases. Conclusions GAS temporal pyomyositis should be considered in children presenting with AOM and painful temporal swelling. Imaging is crucial for diagnosis and assessment of disease extent. Surgical management should be individualized.

title: Parasitic Infections of the Lacrimal System: A Major Review of Etiology, Clinical Presentation, and Management.
abstract: Purpose Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare and often under-recognized causes of lacrimal pathology. Their clinical presentation frequently mimics more common conditions such as chronic dacryocystitis, leading to diagnostic challenges and delays in appropriate management. This study aims to systematically review the literature on parasitic infections of the lacrimal system and to characterize their etiology, clinical presentation, diagnostic approaches, management strategies, and outcomes. Methods A systematic review was conducted across MEDLINE, Embase, Emcare, and PubMed from inception to March 2026. Studies reporting parasitic infections involving the lacrimal apparatus were included. Data on demographics, clinical presentation, anatomical involvement, causative organisms, diagnostic methods, treatment, and outcomes were extracted. Due to heterogeneity and predominance of case reports and small series, a qualitative descriptive analysis was performed. Results A total of 44 studies comprising 172 cases were included. Rhinosporidium seeberi was the most frequently reported pathogen, accounting for 147 cases (85.5%), followed by Leishmania (8 cases, 4.7%) and Ascaris lumbricoides (7 cases, 4.1%). The lacrimal sac was the most commonly involved site. Clinical presentation was nonspecific, with epiphora and medial canthal swelling predominating. Diagnosis was most often established by histopathology following surgical intervention. Management varied by etiology, with surgical excision commonly used for rhinosporidiosis and mechanical extraction for helminthic infections. Outcomes were generally favorable, although recurrence was reported, particularly in R. seeberi infections. Conclusions Parasitic infections of the lacrimal system are rare but clinically important, with diverse presentations and management approaches. Increased awareness is essential for early diagnosis and appropriate treatment. Further studies with standardized reporting are needed to optimize management strategies.

title: Adaptive Control Point B-Spline Method for Improving Accuracy and Deformation Plausibility in Deep Learning Brain Registration.
abstract: Deformable brain image registration plays a crucial role in aligning and jointly analyzing multi-phase and multi-modal neuroimaging data. However, existing unsupervised deep learning-based registration methods typically predict dense displacement fields directly at the voxel level, which often leads to deformation noise and optimization difficulties due to redundant degrees of freedom. Furthermore, these methods are prone to topological distortions when noise or irrelevant information is present. To address these challenges, we propose a robust B-spline registration post-processing framework with adaptive control point density, which can be seamlessly integrated into mainstream registration architectures for brain analysis. Specifically, we design a Control Point Spacing Predictor (CPSPredictor) that adaptively adjusts the distribution density of control points based on the input images, enabling effective regulation of registration flexibility. By modeling displacements with sparse control points and generating continuous and smooth deformation fields via locally supported B-spline basis functions, the proposed method significantly suppresses folding artifacts and preserves anatomical consistency. Extensive experiments on multiple publicly available brain MRI datasets demonstrate that our approach can be seamlessly integrated into existing mainstream registration frameworks, significantly improving both registration accuracy and the physical plausibility of the transformation. For instance, on the IXI dataset, our method boosts the VoxelMorph baseline's DSC by 2.63% and reduces the number of folding points nearly 69-fold. The resulting registration outputs better align with clinical diagnostic requirements, highlighting the method's robustness and practical application potential.

title: ScanSeg: Policy-Guided Sequential Prompting for Dense Fine-Grained Ultrasound Segmentation.
abstract: Dense fine-grained segmentation on standardized ultrasound planes is clinically essential but remains challenging because multiple anatomical structures coexist under speckle noise, acoustic shadowing, weak boundaries, and partial visibility. Promptable foundation models can produce high-quality masks when queried, but they typically return one structure at a time and lack a mechanism to automatically decide what to segment next and where additional evidence is needed, making single-shot "auto" outputs brittle on complex planes. This paper introduces ScanSeg, a scan-inspired framework that formulates multi-structure ultrasound segmentation as sequential evidence accumulation via a small number of prompted calls. ScanSeg maintains a global per-pixel posterior over classes and iteratively issues prompts to a SAM predictor to obtain structure-specific mask observations with confidence scores. Each observation is fused into the posterior through a stable logit-space evidence accumulation rule, preserving global competition among structures. To enable efficient scanning, a lightweight proposal policy is learned to select the next target structure and prompt location conditioned on the current posterior and its uncertainty, trained by supervised imitation from step-wise oracle actions defined by posterior residuals. Experiments on dense abdominal and fetal cardiac ultrasound planes demonstrate that ScanSeg consistently outperforms both single-shot and prompted baselines, yielding more reliable fine-grained multi-structure segmentation and improving average Dice by up to 6.52 points on Abdomen and 4.94 points on A4C with only a few predictor calls.

title: Acute Perinatal Stroke Characteristics and Outcome in Southern Finland.
abstract: Aim Perinatal stroke can cause lifelong morbidities. Outcome prediction is important for parental guidance and follow-up. We studied characteristics of acute perinatal stroke in a Finnish cohort. Methods We performed a population-based study, identifying infants with acute neonatal cerebral ischemia or sinovenous thrombosis (CSVT) in Southern Finland from 2010 to 2023. We analysed the incidence of stroke types, seizures, anti-seizure medication use, and outcomes. Results Altogether 88 infants (1 in 3101 live births) were diagnosed with acute perinatal stroke: 67% with arterial ischemic stroke (AIS), 22% with hemorrhagic stroke (HS) and 11% with CSVT. Seizures and anti-seizure medication use occurred in 78% of infants. Cranial ultrasound infrequently recognized AIS but usually noted haemorrhage. During follow-up, 34% of infants had no adverse outcome diagnosis. The most common outcome was cerebral palsy (CP, 35%). A combination of CP with epilepsy or seizures was more frequent in infants with AIS than in those with other stroke types. Conclusion The distribution of stroke types, symptoms, and adverse outcomes aligns with the previous literature. Acute seizures were common in AIS and HS patients. No recurrent strokes occurred during follow-up and underlying infant-related etiologies were rarely identified.

title: Gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine with and without aura: A multimodal MRI and JuSpace analysis.
abstract: Objective To characterize gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine without aura (MwoA) and migraine with aura (MwA) relative to healthy controls (HC), test direct differences between the migraine groups, and examine spatial associations between voxel-based morphometry findings and molecular and cellular reference templates. Background Structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have reported gray and white matter abnormalities in migraine, but findings vary across cohorts, imaging methods, and clinical subgroups. Whether migraine with and without aura show distinct structural patterns remains uncertain, and the molecular and cellular context of these alterations is incompletely understood. Methods This cross-sectional group-comparison analysis was embedded in an ongoing prospective single-center study at The First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University in Dalian, China, and included participants recruited from August 2025 to March 2026. Thirty HC, 40 participants with MwoA, and 15 participants with MwA underwent T1-weighted and diffusion MRI. Diffusion tensor imaging, neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging, and diffusional kurtosis imaging metrics were analyzed using tract-based spatial statistics; gray matter microstructure and volume were assessed using gray matter-based spatial statistics and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). JuSpace Toolbox correlated unthresholded VBM statistical parametric t (spmT) maps with neurotransmitter- and cell-related templates. Models adjusted for age, sex, and education; VBM additionally adjusted for total intracranial volume; and direct MwoA-versus-MwA sensitivity models included Patient Health Questionnaire-9. Results Relative to HC, MwoA showed higher mean and radial diffusivity and lower neurite density index, whereas MwA showed lower free-water fraction (all threshold-free cluster enhancement-family-wise error [FWE], p < 0.05). No diffusional kurtosis imaging or corrected gray matter-based spatial statistics result was significant. VBM showed lower gray matter volume in MwoA in left cerebellar Crus I (77 voxels; peak-level whole-brain family-wise error (FWE)-corrected p value (pFWE) = 0.022) and right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (6 voxels; pFWE = 0.025), and in MwA in right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (85 voxels; pFWE = 0.019). Direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant in primary and Patient Health Questionnaire-9-adjusted models. JuSpace identified seven and 11 false discovery rate (FDR)-significant neurotransmitter-related associations for MwoA-versus-HC and MwA-versus-HC, respectively; no cell-related template survived FDR correction for MwoA-versus-HC, whereas nine survived for MwA-versus-HC (q < 0.05). No region of interest-clinical association survived Bonferroni correction. Conclusion Multimodal MRI identified gray and white matter alterations in both migraine groups relative to HC, whereas direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant. JuSpace provided complementary spatial context for the VBM findings. These results broaden the structural characterization of migraine but do not establish imaging differences between the two migraine groups.

To characterize gray and white matter structural alterations in migraine without aura (MwoA) and migraine with aura (MwA) relative to healthy controls (HC), test direct differences between the migraine groups, and examine spatial associations between voxel-based morphometry findings and molecular and cellular reference templates.

Background

Structural and diffusion magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) studies have reported gray and white matter abnormalities in migraine, but findings vary across cohorts, imaging methods, and clinical subgroups. Whether migraine with and without aura show distinct structural patterns remains uncertain, and the molecular and cellular context of these alterations is incompletely understood.

Methods

This cross-sectional group-comparison analysis was embedded in an ongoing prospective single-center study at The First Affiliated Hospital of Dalian Medical University in Dalian, China, and included participants recruited from August 2025 to March 2026. Thirty HC, 40 participants with MwoA, and 15 participants with MwA underwent T1-weighted and diffusion MRI. Diffusion tensor imaging, neurite orientation dispersion and density imaging, and diffusional kurtosis imaging metrics were analyzed using tract-based spatial statistics; gray matter microstructure and volume were assessed using gray matter-based spatial statistics and voxel-based morphometry (VBM). JuSpace Toolbox correlated unthresholded VBM statistical parametric t (spmT) maps with neurotransmitter- and cell-related templates. Models adjusted for age, sex, and education; VBM additionally adjusted for total intracranial volume; and direct MwoA-versus-MwA sensitivity models included Patient Health Questionnaire-9.

Results

Relative to HC, MwoA showed higher mean and radial diffusivity and lower neurite density index, whereas MwA showed lower free-water fraction (all threshold-free cluster enhancement-family-wise error [FWE], p < 0.05). No diffusional kurtosis imaging or corrected gray matter-based spatial statistics result was significant. VBM showed lower gray matter volume in MwoA in left cerebellar Crus I (77 voxels; peak-level whole-brain family-wise error (FWE)-corrected p value (pFWE) = 0.022) and right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (6 voxels; pFWE = 0.025), and in MwA in right inferior frontal gyrus, pars triangularis (85 voxels; pFWE = 0.019). Direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant in primary and Patient Health Questionnaire-9-adjusted models. JuSpace identified seven and 11 false discovery rate (FDR)-significant neurotransmitter-related associations for MwoA-versus-HC and MwA-versus-HC, respectively; no cell-related template survived FDR correction for MwoA-versus-HC, whereas nine survived for MwA-versus-HC (q < 0.05). No region of interest-clinical association survived Bonferroni correction.

Conclusion

Multimodal MRI identified gray and white matter alterations in both migraine groups relative to HC, whereas direct MwoA-versus-MwA comparisons were nonsignificant. JuSpace provided complementary spatial context for the VBM findings. These results broaden the structural characterization of migraine but do not establish imaging differences between the two migraine groups.

title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice.
abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer's disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2-magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer-MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.
